title: upgrade: FlashAttentionV2 kernel update + rope/rotary fused ops + KV-continuous-batching scheduling
author: Ava Morales
description:
Motivation: Upgrade our attention kernels to the FlashAttentionV2 variants and introduce fused rope/rotary computation paths to reduce per-token kernel launches and memory traffic. This PR also adds scheduling heuristics to better place KV-cache-backed requests in continuous batching windows, reducing stall time for interactive workloads.

Summary of changes:
- Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels with a fallback to existing kernels when not supported on-target GPUs.
- Implement fused rope/rotary pre- and post-attention ops to eliminate separate elementwise kernels for rotary embedding application.
- Extend KV cache layout to support contiguous per-sequence packing that pairs with continuous batching logic.
- Scheduler changes: new policy to coalesce small KV requests into a dedicated low-latency lane and bump larger batched requests to a throughput lane. Includes heuristics based on sequence length, token arrival rate, and model config.
- Profiling + microbenchmarks and integration tests to validate latency and throughput improvements.

Checklist:
- [x] FlashAttentionV2 kernels added and feature-flagged
- [x] Fused rope/rotary ops implemented and tested
- [x] KV cache packing + compatibility with existing snapshots
- [x] Scheduler policy and config knobs wired into runtime
- [x] Microbenchmarks demonstrating latency improvements for 1-8 token increments
- [x] Docs added to perf/ and a short migration note

Compatibility notes: The new kernels are behind a runtime feature flag (ATTN_FLASHV2=true). On older drivers or unsupported hardware we fall back to the prior kernels. KV cache format change is versioned; the system supports dual-format reads during a migration window.

Risks & mitigations: Fused ops increase register pressure on some Ampere-class cards; we added a kernel selection path that prefers the lower-pressure implementation when the occupancy budget is exceeded. Scheduler heuristics have guardrails (rate limits and backoff) to avoid thrashing between lanes.

This PR is primarily performance-focused but includes a couple of small API surface changes (runtime config knobs) documented in docs/perf/flashattn-upgrade.md.

release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rope/rotary ops; improved latency for short interactive sequences via KV-continuous-batching and scheduler lane coalescing. Feature gated behind ATTN_FLASHV2.
